messages:
incident-bot: :rotating_light: ALERT: dedpool-mstrl-01 node heartbeat missed >3x (gpu-4432). Severity: P2. Affected tenant: MistralCorp (dedicated). Links: https://console/redwood/incidents/1945009999

alice (oncall): seeing elevated error rate for MistralCorp routes, small spike in token failures. Pls confirm impact scope.

ben (sre): I can see 4432 flapping in the host manager. Node lost heartbeat at 1945009953, kube shows NotReady. Some pods on that node failed to reattach to KV cache.

mira (cust-eng): MistralCorp reporting higher latency and a couple of 5xxs on their dedicated endpoints. They opened a ticket referencing our incident id. They asked for ETA and whether isolation is possible.

carla (solutions): their SLAs are strict. We should prefer live migration + quick drain rather than full pool fallback if possible. Can we isolate only affected tenant instances?

derek (eng-runtime): we have a per-tenant placement affinity in this pool but some replicas are spread. Quick plan: 1) cordon node, 2) drain non-critical replicas, 3) live-migrate critical replicas to hot standby nodes in same pool, 4) if migration stalls, failover those replicas to compatible model variants.

alice (oncall): ok executing cordon now: `dedpoolctl cordon --pool dedpool-mstrl-01 --node gpu-4432`

ben (sre): confirmed cordon complete. Node is marked unschedulable. Starting drain with `dedpoolctl drain-node --node gpu-4432 --grace 30s --ignore-cache`

carla (solutions): note: leave at least one replica for control-plane hooks; don't evict all caches simultaneously.

ben (sre): drain started. Evicting non-critical jobs first. Drain progress: 3/7 replicas moved. One migration hitting KV reattach timeout.

mira (cust-eng): I'm on call with MistralCorp. Told them we're initiating a graded drain to avoid full outage. They asked if we can prioritize their inference jobs over background batch.

alice (oncall): pushed a priority label to their live-realtime pods: `kubectl label pod <pod> redwood.priority=high` — been queued to scheduler.

ben (sre): migration resumed. Live replicas moved to gpu-4436 and gpu-4421. One background batch job stuck due to stale disk mount, cancelling it.

derek (eng-runtime): seeing repeated ECC logs on GPU 4432: `GPU ECC single-bit error rate rising` — looks hardware. Recommend replace node after warm reboot.

carla (solutions): can we avoid a full pool fallback? Customer asked specifically not to fail traffic to other regions.

elaine (acct-ops): FYI MistralCorp has a dedicated support SLA. I'll draft a short incident note to share — ETA for next update in 15m.

ben (sre): drain complete: 7/7 replicas moved or evicted. No more pods on gpu-4432. Marked node drained at 1945011400.

alice (oncall): initiating replacement workflow: `infractl replace-node --node gpu-4432 --pool dedpool-mstrl-01 --reason "ECC errors"`

incident-bot: ACTION: page infra-oncall. Pager sent to @dylan-infra.

dylan-infra: got the page, pulling console logs. Confirming scheduled maintenance window?

derek (eng-runtime): not a scheduled maint. We should do a cold power-cycle first; if ECC persists, swap GPU unit.

dylan-infra: power-cycle attempted remotely, node came back but kernel reported driver ECC raise at boot, same device id. Opening hardware ticket with cloud provider to replace instance.

mira (cust-eng): MistralCorp noted slight request retrying but overall traffic is 'mostly normal' now. Thanking team for quick migration.

carla (solutions): follow-up action: create canary synthetic check for their top 10 prompt sets. Derek, can runtime add a KV reattach metric alert?

derek (eng-runtime): yes will add alert: `kv.reattach.failures > 5/min` -> page eng-oncall.

elaine (acct-ops): sending customer note: "We've isolated the issue to a single GPU node (4432) in your dedicated pool, migrated your live workloads with no data loss, and are replacing the hardware. We'll update when replacement is complete." Will attach timeline and reconciliation.

ben (sre): cloud provider confirmed replacement in progress; expected completion + verification by 1945013500.

alice (oncall): marking incident as mitigated for customer traffic. Moving to monitoring phase. Will keep thread open until replacement verified and node removed from pool.

mira (cust-eng): MistralCorp appreciates transparency. They want a postmortem and a note on 'how to avoid future flaps' — I suggested improved proactive ECC thresholds and a maintenance preemptive replacement policy.

carla (solutions): logging follow-up item: add a pool-level config to auto-replace nodes after 3 ECC events in 24h. Filing JIRA RW-7684.

ben (sre): verification: no 5xxs in last 5m for MistralCorp endpoints. KV cache hit ratio stable.

dylan-infra: provider reports replacement instance ready, performing verification checks. GPU health OK on new node.

alice (oncall): node gpu-4432 permanently removed from pool at 1945013560; replacement attached as gpu-4490. Updating slack channel and customer.

incident-bot: INCIDENT STATUS: mitigated -> monitoring. Severity downgraded to P3.

elaine (acct-ops): sent formal summary to MistralCorp and their CSM.

mira (cust-eng): customer requested PM with timeline + action items. I'll coordinate with Derek and Ben.

carla (solutions): nice coordinated run. Small note: add runbook step for per-tenant priority label automation during drains.

alice (oncall): thanks everyone. I'll close when postmortem draft is ready.

ben (sre): leaving a short debug log here for postmortem: ```
Node: gpu-4432
Events: heartbeat miss -> kube NotReady -> ECC errors triggered -> drain -> replacement
Timeframe: 1945009953 - 1945013560
Resolution: live-migration, node replacement, KV attach alert added
```

incident-bot: Thread closed for updates after confirmation.
